'''Robin Lyth Hudson''' (4 May 1940 – 12 January 2021) was a British mathematician notable for his contribution to [[quantum probability]].

==Education and career==
Hudson received his Ph.D. from the [[University of Oxford]] in 1966 under [[John T. Lewis]] with a thesis entitled ''Generalised Translation-Invariant Mechanics''. He was appointed assistant lecturer at the University of Nottingham in 1964, promoted to a chair in 1985 and served as head of department from 1987 to 1990. He spent sabbatical semesters in Heidelberg (1978), [[University of Texas at Austin|Austin, Texas]] (1983), and [[University of Colorado Boulder|Colorado Boulder]] (1996). After taking early retirement in 1997, he held part-time research posts at Nottingham Trent University (1997–2005), the Slovak Academy
of Sciences (1997–2000) and Loughborough University (2005–21), and a visiting professorship at the University of Łódź (2002) which awarded him an honorary doctorate in 2013.

Hudson was a mathematical physicist who was one of the pioneers of [[quantum probability]]. An early result,<ref>{{cite journal|last=Hudson|first=R. L.|title=When is the Wigner quasi-probability density non-negative?|journal=Reports on Mathematical Physics|year=1974|volume=6|issue=2|pages=249–252|doi=10.1016/0034-4877(74)90007-x|bibcode=1974RpMP....6..249H}}</ref> now known as Hudson's theorem in quantum optics, shows that the pure quantum states with positive [[Wigner quasiprobability distribution]] are the Gaussian ones. Together with PhD students, Hudson established one of the first quantum central limit theorems,<ref>{{cite journal|last=Cushen|first=C. D.|author2=Hudson, R. L.|title=A quantum-mechanical central limit theorem|journal=Journal of Applied Probability|year=1971|volume=8|issue=3 |pages=454–469|doi=10.2307/3212170 |jstor=3212170 |s2cid=123936481 }}</ref> proved an early quantum de Finetti theorem,<ref>{{cite journal|last=Hudson|first=R. L.|author2=Moody, G. R.|title=Locally normal symmetric states and an analogue of de Finetti's Theorem|journal=Zeitschrift für Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie und Verwandte Gebiete|year=1976|volume=33|issue=4 |pages=343–351|doi=10.1007/BF00534784 |s2cid=122364811 |doi-access=free}}</ref> and introduced quantum Brownian motion<ref>{{cite journal|last=Cockcroft|first=A. M.|author2=Hudson, R. L.|title=Quantum mechanical Wiener processes|year=1977|journal=Journal of Multivariate Analysis|volume=7|pages=107–124|doi=10.1016/0047-259X(77)90035-5 |doi-access=free}}</ref> as a non-commuting pair of families of unbounded operators, using the formalism of quantum field theory. He collaborated with [[K. R. Parthasarathy (probabilist)|K. R. Parthasarathy]] first at the [[University of Manchester]], and later at [[University of Nottingham]] and at [[Loughborough University]], on their seminal work in [[quantum stochastic calculus]].<ref>{{cite web|last=D. Applebaum|title=Robin Hudson's Pathless Path to Quantum Stochastic Calculus|url=https://www.applebaum.staff.shef.ac.uk/Hudpath.pdf|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304061146/https://www.applebaum.staff.shef.ac.uk/Hudpath.pdf|archivedate=2016-03-04}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author1-link=Jinqiao Duan|author1=Jinqiao Duan |author2=Shunlong Luo |author3=Caishi Wang |title=Recent development in stochastic dynamics and stochastic analysis|year=2010|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=978-9814277266|page=preface-x}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=[[K. R. Parthasarathy (probabilist)|K. R. Parthasarathy]]|title=Quantum Stochastic Calculus|url=https://www.mathunion.org/Publications/Bulletins/39/parthasarathy.ps|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120728070024/http://www.mathunion.org/Publications/Bulletins/39/parthasarathy.ps|archivedate=2012-07-28}}</ref>

In later papers he developed a theory of quantum stochastic double product integrals and their application to the quantum [[Yang–Baxter equation]], the quantisation of [[Lie bialgebra]]s and quantum Lévy area.<ref>Hudson, R. L.; Pulmannová, S. (2004). "Double product integrals and Enriquez quantisation of Lie bialgebras I: The quasitriangularity relations". Journal of Mathematical Physics. 45: 2090–2105.</ref>
